questions.question: What is the name of the thermionic electron tube used to oscillate and amplify microwave frequency signals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Klystron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Klystron:-**

 
 
• It is a vacuum tube that uses the interaction of an electron beam and electromagnetic waves to generate or amplify microwave signals.
 
• The name of the thermionic electron tube used to oscillate and amplify microwave frequency signals is Klystron.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beam tetrodes:-**

 
 
• These are also vacuum tubes used for amplification, but they are not specifically designed for microwave frequencies and do not have the same level of precision as Klystrons.
 
 
 
• **Thyratrons:-**
 
 
• These are also vacuum tubes, but they are used for controlling high-power circuits and not for generating or amplifying microwave signals.
 
 
 
• **Neutrino:-**
 
 
• It is a subatomic particle that has nothing to do with vacuum tubes or microwave signals.

questions.question: Which potassium acid salt is obtained as a by - product of alcohol manufacture during the fermentation process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium bitartrate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium bitartrate** is the by-product of the** fermentation of grape juice** or** other fruit juices** during the **alcohol-making process.**
 
• It is also known as **cream of tartar.**
 
• It is a **white crystalline powder** that is commonly used in baking as a** leavening agent **and to **stabilize egg whites.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potassium citrate** is a salt that is commonly used as a **food additive **and in medical treatments to **prevent kidney stones.**

 
 
• If you suffer from **chronic kidney failure**, you should avoid using potassium citrate.
 
 
 
• **Potassium nitrate,** also known as** saltpeter,** is a chemical compound that is used in **fertilizers, fireworks, and as a food preservative.**
 
 
• It exists as the** mineral niter** in nature.
 
• It is a **source of nitrogen**, which bears niter's name.
 
 
 
• **Potassium hydrogen adipate** is a salt that is used in the manufacture of **synthetic fibers and plastics.**
 
 
• It's a chemical substance found in a variety of powders used to make** fruit-flavored or jelly-like desserts and drinks.**

questions.question: What test is used where the elements present in the compound are converted from covalent form into the ionic form by fusing the compound with sodium metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Lassaigne's test.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lassaigne's test** is a general test for the detection of halogens, nitrogen, and sulfur in an organic compound.
 
• These elements are covalently bonded to the organic compounds. 
 
• In order to detect them, these have to be converted into their ionic forms.
 
• This is done by fusing the organic compound with sodium metal. This is done by fusing the organic compound with sodium metal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A flame test is an analytical procedure used in chemistry to detect the presence of certain elements, primarily metal ions, based on each element's characteristic emission spectrum. 
 
• A D-dimer test looks for D-dimer in blood. D-dimer is a protein fragment (small piece) that's made when a blood clot dissolves in your body.

questions.question: Which among the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **__CaO__**

__
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO)** has a **highest** **boiling point.**
 
• It undergoes a process called **calcination,** where it is heated to **very high temperatures (around 2,572°C or 4,662°F)** to convert it into **calcium oxide.**
 
• However, **calcium oxide** does not boil as a pure substance at atmospheric pressure since it undergoes thermal decomposition before reaching its **boiling point.**

 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO),** also known as **quicklime or burnt lime**, is an **inorganic compound composed of calcium and oxygen**.
 
• Chemical Formula: **CaO**
 
• Molar Mass: 56.08 g/mol

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance: Calcium oxide** is a **white, caustic, crystalline solid at room temperature.**
 
• **Melting Point:** The melting point of calcium oxide is approximately **2,572°C (4,662°F)**, indicating its solid state at normal conditions.
 
• **Boiling Point: Calcium oxide **does not have a distinct boiling point because it undergoes thermal decomposition before reaching its boiling point.
 
• When heated,** calcium oxide **decomposes into** calcium hydroxide** and releases **oxygen gas.**

questions.question: What is the product of the reaction when anhydrite undergoes hydration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gypsum.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anhydrite** is a mineral that has the chemical formula** CaSO₄.**
 
• It is an** anhydrous form** of gypsum.
 
• When anhydrite undergoes **hydration**, it reacts with water to form gypsum (CaSO₄.2H₂O).
 
• Therefore, the product of the reaction when **anhydrite undergoes** hydration is gypsum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum **is a **soft sulfate mineral** that is widely used in construction as a building material.

 
 
• It is also used in **agriculture, medicine, and other industries.**
 
 
 
• **Limonite** is a type of** iron ore** that is **brownish-yellow** in color.
 
 
• It can precipitate from surface or groundwater that is rich in iron, and it forms from the **weathering **of other iron minerals.
 
 
 
• **Magnesite** is a mineral that has the chemical formula **MgCO₃**.
 
 
• The mineral was created either by the action of magnesium-containing solutions on** calcite **or as an alteration product from rocks rich in magnesium.
 
 
 
• **Kaolin** is a type of clay mineral that is used in **ceramics, paper,** and other industries.
 
 
• The fine particle size, plate-like or **lamellar particle shape**, and chemical inertness of hydrous kaolin are its distinguishing features.

__
 
• The chemical compound having the molecular formula **C₃H₄O **is called **Acrolein.**
 
• Acrolein is mostly used for the production of **acrylic acid and acrylate ester.**
 
• **Acrylic acid **is used in the production of various products such as **adhesives, coatings, and paints.**
 
• **Acrylate ester** is used in the production of **polymers and plastics.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naphthaldehyde** is an organic compound that is used as a** flavoring agent.**

 
 
• It is also used in the production of** dyes and pharmaceuticals.**
 
 
 
• **Vanillin** is an organic compound that is used as a** flavoring agent** in food and beverages.
 
 
• It is the main ingredient in the **vanilla bean extract.**
 
 
 
• **Muscone** is an organic compound that is used in the production of** perfumes and fragrances.**
